paragraphs: We provide modular and scalable equipment-based solutions for power generation, control and distribution, and the management of raw materials in oil and natural gas well completions. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Solaris serves multiple U.S. end markets, including data center, energy, and other commercial and industrial sectors.
We operate through two reportable business segments:

•Solaris Power Solutions: This segment delivers power generation, control, and distribution solutions. Our offerings support data center, energy, and other commercial and industrial sector customers by providing flexible, on-demand power infrastructure, including power control and distribution capabilities.

•Solaris Logistics Solutions: This segment designs and manufactures specialized equipment that enables the efficient management of raw materials used in the completion of oil and natural gas wells. Our equipment-based logistics services include field technician support, software solutions, and may also include last mile and mobilization services.
We own or lease various facilities, including our corporate headquarters in Houston, Texas, and the following segment-specific facilities:

Solaris Power Solutions. As part of the acquisition of Mobile Energy Rentals, LLC ("MER" and such acquisition, the "MER Acquisition"), we obtained access to a long-standing relationship with a leading supplier of distributed power generation equipment. This supplier provides a significant portion of the equipment used in this segment's operations. While recent commercial dialogue with this supplier remains strong, as evidenced by our numerous significant purchase orders placed with this supplier, there is risk that we may not be able to secure additional supply of power generation capacity in a timely or cost-effective manner. While we believe that viable market alternatives to this vendor exist, there is no guarantee that we would not be exposed to supply chain shortages or price increases in the future.

Solaris Logistics Solutions. We have built long-term relationships with third-party suppliers for the transportation of equipment and products, as well as for the provision of materials used in the manufacturing and maintenance of our systems. Although we do not currently have long-term agreements with third-party trucking suppliers, we have consistently relied on these suppliers over extended periods, which has enabled us to obtain trucking services on a timely basis. While

we believe that we can make satisfactory alternative arrangements in the event of any interruption in the supply of third-party trucking services, there is no guarantee that we will be able to avoid shortages or price increases in the future.

Solaris Power Solutions. Revenue in this segment is currently significantly dependent on a single data center customer, which made up 88% and 96%, respectively, of total segment revenue for the years ended December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024.

In 2025, we entered into a long-term commercial arrangement with this customer to provide up to approximately 900 megawatts of power generation capacity to support its data center. The commercial contract has an initial term of seven years. Revenue under this arrangement is expected to commence in 2026. In connection with this arrangement, we and the customer formed Stateline Power, LLC, which is owned 50.1% by us and 49.9% by the customer.

During the first quarter of 2026, we entered into a rental agreement with an affiliate of an investment grade, global technology company and industry leader in the evolving artificial intelligence computer space to provide over 500 megawatts of power generation equipment to support the customer's power demand for artificial intelligence computing needs at its data center. The agreement's initial term of ten years is expected to commence in 2027.

Solaris Logistics Solutions. The customer base within this segment primarily consists of major exploration and production ("E&P") companies, as well as oilfield services companies. We typically engage with our customers through Master Service Agreements ("MSAs"), which outline the key terms of our arrangements. Individual work orders, which define the scope and specific service to be performed, are issued under the framework of these MSAs. For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, one customer accounted for 28% and 20%, respectively, of total revenue in this segment. Additionally, another customer represented 12% and 13% of total revenue in this segment for the same periods.

Solaris Power Solutions. The majority of the distributed energy we provide occurs off-grid or "behind-the-meter" and is often seen as an alternative to grid-based power when grid access is either unavailable, delayed or viewed as unreliable. Behind-the-meter power can also be viewed by some customers as a compliment to the grid as it can provide a diversified energy source and an extra layer of backup once grid connection is received. Therefore, our primary competition for our offering is the electricity grid, but we can also work in conjunction with the grid. There are also numerous other distributed energy companies that offer both similar and different technologies. Each customer's application can favor one technology over another, so not all technologies or companies are in direct competition, and as is the case with grid power, can even be complimentary offerings. The majority of distributed energy companies today are privately held, and competition tends to be very fragmented at smaller generator sizes. Only a few companies have similar capabilities as Solaris to provide an integrated distributed power solution on large, behind-the meter power applications.

Solaris Logistics Solutions. The oil and natural gas services industry is highly competitive. We have numerous types of competitors, including logistics companies, equipment manufacturers, hydraulic fracturing service companies and sand mining companies. Some of these companies could be customers of ours on certain jobs while also utilizing their own equipment and integrated service offerings on other jobs.

headings: Risks Related to Our Operations and Industry
Distributed power generation services in some applications compete with access to the grid.
We expect to face significant competition in the future as the distributed power industry evolves.
Reliance upon a small number of large customers may adversely affect our revenue and operating results.
We are subject to a number of risks associated with Stateline.
Our Power Solutions segment is dependent on our relationships with key suppliers to obtain equipment.
Many of our power systems involve long sales cycles.
Our customers may not continue to outsource their power system needs.
The volatility of oil and natural gas prices may adversely affect the demand for our systems, products and services, and negatively impact our results of operations.
Tariffs and other trade measures could adversely affect our results of operations, financial position and cash flows.
We engage in transactions with related parties and such transactions present possible conflicts of interest that could have an adverse effect on us.
Technological advancements in the products and technologies we provide could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We are subject to cybersecurity risks. A cyber incident could occur and result in information theft, data corruption, operational disruption and/or financial loss.
We rely on a few key employees whose absence or loss could adversely affect our business.
We are subject to extensive government laws and regulations concerning our employees, and the cost of compliance with such laws and regulations could be material.
Unsatisfactory safety performance may negatively affect our customer relationships and, to the extent we fail to retain existing customers or attract new customers, adversely impact our revenues.
Risks Related to Financial Condition

Our business depends on domestic capital spending by the industries we service, and reductions in capital spending could have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, results of operations and financial condition.
We may be adversely affected by uncertainty in the global financial markets or the deterioration of the financial condition, and resulting credit risk, of our customers.
Our ability to use our net operating loss ("NOL") carryovers may be limited.
Risks Related to Regulatory Matters
We are subject to environmental and occupational health and safety laws and regulations that may expose us to significant costs and liabilities.
Increased attention to sustainability matters may impact our business.
Anti-indemnity provisions enacted by many states may restrict or prohibit a party's indemnification of us.
Changes to applicable tax laws and regulations or exposure to additional income tax liabilities could affect our operating results and cash flows.
Risks Related to Our Class A Common Stock
Our stock price could be volatile, and you may not be able to resell shares of your Class A common stock at or above the price you paid.
paragraphs: The following are certain risk factors that affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows. Many of these risks are beyond our control. These risk factors should be considered in connection with evaluating the forward-looking statements contained in this Annual Report. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones that we face. If any of the events described below were to actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows could be adversely affected and our results could differ materially from expected and historical results, any of which may also adversely affect the holders of our stock.

We may be unable to adapt our distributed power technologies to meet increasing customer needs and power loads, which could result in increased downtime of our power generation offering and disruptions to the power supply to our customers.

Demand for power has continued to significantly outpace available power generation supply from the grid, with the electrification of the oil and natural gas industry, as an example, straining aging and unreliable power grids. Further, the expanding use of artificial intelligence has led to the expansion of existing data centers and plans for new data centers.

As we expand our distributed power offering, the possibility exists that our current offering may not be able to effectively manage related power loads, resulting in potential downtimes and disruptions for our customers. Such experiences could have a material adverse effect on our business and operating results due to the damage to our reputation and the resulting dissatisfaction of customers. If we are unable to adapt our power generation technologies to meet future demand and customer needs as they evolve, or otherwise unable to meet their reliability requirements, our business and operating results may be adversely effected.

Distributed power generation services are an alternative for customers to consider when grid access is unavailable, costly or delayed. Our distributed power offering could be affected in the event that large-scale utility projects are completed and the associated transmission and distribution networks are established. In this case, customers may only use our offering as backup power or bridge power until line power is received.

The landscape of the distributed power industry is evolving rapidly, driven by increased demand from numerous end-markets, including those in the data center and energy businesses. As a result, increased competition from within the distributed power industry can likely be expected to occur. Should this materialize, the portion of the total addressable market that we could capture with our Power Solutions segment will be lower than expected which could translate to lower than expected revenues.

paragraphs: We provide modular and scalable equipment-based solutions for power generation, power control and distribution, and the management of raw materials in oil and natural gas well completions. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Solaris serves multiple U.S. end markets, including data center, energy, and other commercial and industrial sectors.

During 2025, we expanded our power solutions platform through the acquisition of HVMVLV, LLC, which enhanced our capabilities in power control and distribution and strengthened our distributed power generation offerings.
We operate through two reportable business segments:

•Solaris Power Solutions: This segment delivers power generation, power control, and power distribution solutions. Our offerings support data center, energy, and other commercial and industrial sector customers by providing flexible, on-demand power infrastructure, including power control and distribution capabilities.

•Solaris Logistics Solutions: This segment designs and manufactures specialized equipment that enables the efficient management of raw materials used in the completion of oil and natural gas wells. Our equipment-based logistics services include field technician support, software solutions, and may also include last mile and mobilization services.

On August 15, 2025, we acquired HVMVLV, LLC ("HVMVLV"), a specialty provider of power control and distribution solutions. The acquisition expanded the Company's capabilities in power control and distribution, enhancing its distributed power generation offerings within the Solaris Power Solutions segment. The results of HVMVLV's operations have been included in our consolidated financial statements from the acquisition date through December 31, 2025. For further details regarding the acquisition, refer to Note 4. "Business Combinations" in the notes to our consolidated financial statements.

On October 8, 2025, we issued $747.5 million aggregate principal amount of 0.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2031 (the "2031 Notes") in an underwritten public offering. We used a portion of the net proceeds to repay in full and terminate our existing senior secured term loan (the "Term Loan"), including its related accrued interest and applicable prepayment penalties. This repayment resulted in a loss on debt extinguishment of $41.5 million, which was recognized in the fourth quarter of 2025. We also entered into capped call transactions to reduce potential dilution from conversions. The 2031 Notes provide lower-cost, longer-term financing to support growth in our Solaris Power Solutions segment. Refer to Note 12. "Convertible Notes" in the notes to our consolidated financial statements for additional information regarding the terms of the 2031 Notes.
Additional Borrowings under Stateline Term Loan

During the fourth quarter of 2025, Stateline drew an additional $114.0 million under its term loan facility, increasing the outstanding balance to $186.0 million. The proceeds were used to fund growth-related capital expenditures. For additional information on the Stateline term loan facility, refer to Note 11. "Debt" in the notes to our consolidated financial statements.

On February 12, 2026, the Company entered into a Master Equipment Rental Agreement (the "Agreement") with Hatchbo, LLC (the "Customer") to provide over 500 megawatts of power generation equipment to support the Customer's power demand for artificial intelligence computing needs at its data center. The Customer is an affiliate of an investment grade, global technology company and industry leader in the evolving artificial intelligence computer space. For additional information on the Agreement, refer to Note 21. "Subsequent Events" in the notes to our consolidated financial statements.

paragraphs: 本公司提供模組化且可擴充的設備基礎解決方案，用於電力產生、控制與分配，以及油氣井完井過程中的原材料管理。總部設於德克薩斯州休士頓市，Solaris 服務多個美國終端市場，包括資料中心、能源及其他商業與工業部門。
本公司透過兩個應報告分部運營：
•Solaris Power Solutions：此分部提供電力產生、控制與分配解決方案。我們的產品支持資料中心、能源及其他商業與工業部門客戶，透過提供靈活的按需電力基礎建設，包括電力控制與分配能力。
•Solaris Logistics Solutions：此分部設計與製造專用設備，用以提高油氣井完井過程中的原材料管理效率。我們的設備基礎物流服務包括現場技術人員支援、軟體解決方案，也可能包含最後一哩與動員服務。
本公司擁有或租賃多種設施，包括位於德克薩斯州休士頓市的總部，以及以下分部專用設施：

Solaris Power Solutions。作為收購 Mobile Energy Rentals, LLC（"MER" 以及此收購，稱為 "MER Acquisition"）的一部分，我們取得與一家領先的分散式電力產生設備供應商的長期關係。此供應商提供此分部運營中使用的大部分設備。雖然近期與此供應商的商業對話依然強勁，如證據所示，我們已下多筆重大採購訂單，但我們仍面臨無法及時或以成本效益方式取得更多電力產生能力的風險。雖然我們認為此供應商的市場替代方案存在，但無法保證我們未來不會面臨供應鏈短缺或價格上漲的風險。
Solaris Logistics Solutions。我們已與第三方供應商建立長期關係，用以設備與產品的運輸，以及用於我們系統製造與維護所需的材料。雖然我們目前沒有與第三方貨運供應商簽訂長期協議，但我們已持續依賴這些供應商長時間，這使我們能及時取得貨運服務。雖然
我們認為在第三方貨運服務供應中斷的情況下，我們可以做出滿意的替代安排，但無法保證我們未來能避免短缺或價格上漲的風險。
Solaris Power Solutions. 本應報告分部的營業收入目前嚴重依賴單一資料中心客戶，該客戶於2025年12月31日財年及2024年12月31日財年，分別佔該應報告分部總營業收入的88%及96%。
2025年，我們與該客戶簽訂長期商業協議，提供最多約900 megawatts 的電力發電容量，以支援其資料中心。該商業契約的初始期限為七年。根據此協議，收入預期於2026年開始。與此協議相關，我們與該客戶共同成立 Stateline Power, LLC，該公司由我們持有50.1%、該客戶持有49.9%。
2026年第一季，我們與一家投資等級、全球科技公司及人工智慧計算領域領導者的子公司簽訂租賃協議，提供超過500 megawatts 的電力發電設備，以支援該客戶資料中心人工智慧計算需求的電力需求。該協議的初始期限為十年，預期於2027年開始。

Solaris Logistics Solutions. 本應報告分部的客戶羣主要由大型探勘與生產（"E&P"）公司以及油井服務公司組成。我們通常透過主服務協議（"MSAs"）與客戶合作，說明我們安排的關鍵條款。個別工作單則是在這些MSAs框架下發出，以明確服務範圍及具體服務內容。於2025年12月31日財年及2024年12月31日財年，單一客戶分別佔該應報告分部總營業收入的28%及20%。此外，另一客戶於相同期間分別佔該應報告分部總營業收入的12%及13%。

Solaris Power Solutions. 我們提供的分散式能源多數為離網或 "behind-the-meter" 類型，常被視為在電網無法使用、延遲或被視為不可靠時的替代方案。對於部分客戶而言，behind-the-meter 電力也可被視為電網的補充，因其可提供多元化的能源來源，並在電網連接後提供額外的備用電力。因此，我們產品的主要競爭對手為電網，但我們也可以與電網合作。此外，還有許多分散式能源公司提供類似或不同的技術。每個客戶的應用場景可能偏好某種技術而非其他技術，因此並非所有技術或公司都直接競爭，甚至可能與電網電力一樣，成為互補的服務。目前大多數分散式能源公司為私人持有，且在較小發電規模時，競爭多為零散且分散。僅有少數公司具備與Solaris相似的能力，可提供整合式的分散式電力解決方案，應用於大型、behind-the-meter 電力需求。
Solaris Logistics Solutions. 油氣服務產業競爭激烈。我們的競爭對手包括物流公司、設備製造商、水力壓裂服務公司及砂礦公司。其中一些公司可能在某些工作中成為我們的客戶，而在其他工作中則會使用自己的設備及整合服務方案。

paragraphs: 本公司提供模組化且可擴充的設備基準解決方案，用於電力發電、電力控制與分配，以及油氣井完井過程中原始材料的管理。總部設於德克薩斯州休士頓市，Solaris 服務多個美國終端市場，包括資料中心、能源及其他商業與工業部門。
2025 年，本公司透過收購 HVMVLV, LLC，擴充了電力解決方案平台，這項收購增強了本公司在電力控制與分配的技術能力，並強化了本公司在分散式電力發電解決方案的提供。
本公司透過兩個應報告分部運作：
•Solaris Power Solutions：此分部提供電力發電、電力控制與電力分配解決方案。本公司產品支持資料中心、能源及其他商業與工業部門客戶，提供彈性且按需的電力基礎建設，包括電力控制與分配能力。
•Solar, Logistics Solutions：此分部設計與製造專門設備，用以提高油氣井完井過程中原始材料管理的效率。本公司基於設備的物流服務包括現場技術支援、軟體解決方案，也可能包含最後一哩與動員服務。

2025 年 8 月 15 日，本公司收購 HVMVLV, LLC（"HVMVLV"），一家專門提供電力控制與分配解決方案的公司。此收購擴充了本公司在電力控制與分配的技術能力，並強化了 Solaris Power Solutions 分部的分散式電力發電解決方案。自收購日開始，HVMVLV 的營運成果已納入本公司合併財務報表，直至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。有關此收購的更多細節，請參閱財務報表附註中的第 4 節 "企業合併"。

2025 年 10 月 8 日，本公司發行總金額為 7.475 億美元的 0.25% 可轉換優先無擔保債券（"2031 債券"），發行方式為經由經紀商的公開發行。本公司使用部分淨資金償還現有優先無擔保貸款（"貸款"），包括其相關應計利息及適用的提前償還罰款。此償還導致債務終止損失 4,150 萬美元，此損失於 2025 年第四季認列。本公司亦簽訂限額認購合約，以減少因轉換可能產生的稀釋風險。2031 債券提供較低成本、較長期限的融資，以支持本公司 Solaris Power Solutions 分部的成長。有關 2031 債券條款的更多資訊，請參閱財務報表附註中的第 12 節 "可轉換債券"。
Stateline 優先貸款的額外融資
於 2025 年第四季，Stateline 在其定期貸款融資計畫下額外取得 1.14 億美元，使未償還餘額增至 1.86 億美元。所得資金用於支應與成長相關的資本支出。有關 Stateline 定期貸款融資計畫之更多資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表附註之第 11 註："債務"。
2026 年 2 月 12 日，本公司與 Hatchbo, LLC（"客戶"）簽訂主設備租賃協議（"協議"），提供超過 500 兆瓦的電力發電設備，以支援客戶在資料中心針對人工智慧計算需求之電力需求。客戶為一投資等級、全球科技公司之關係企業，並為人工智慧計算領域之產業領導者。有關協議之更多資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表附註之第 21 註："後續事件"。

headings: 與本公司營運及產業相關之風險
在某些應用場合，分散式發電服務與接取電網之服務存在競爭。
隨著分散式發電產業持續演進，本公司預期將面臨顯著的競爭。
對少數大型客戶之依賴可能對本公司營業收入及營運成果產生負面影響。
本公司面臨與Stateline相關之多重風險。
本公司之Power Solutions應報告分部依賴與關鍵供應商之關係以取得設備。
許多本公司之電力系統涉及長銷售週期。
本公司客戶可能不再委外處理其電力系統需求。
油氣價格的波動可能對我們的系統、產品及服務需求產生不利影響，並對我們的營運結果造成負面影響。
關稅及其他貿易措施可能對我們的營運結果、財務狀況及現金流產生不利影響。
我們與關聯方進行交易，而這些交易可能產生利益衝突，對我們產生不利影響。
我們所提供的產品及技術的技術進步可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
我們面臨網路安全風險。網路事件可能發生，導致資訊竊取、資料毀損、營運中斷及/或財務損失。
我們依賴少數關鍵員工，其缺席或離職可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們面臨廣泛的政府法律及法規，有關我們員工的規定，而遵守這些法律及法規的成本可能重大。
不滿意的安全表現可能對我們的客戶關係產生負面影響，若我們未能留住現有客戶或吸引新客戶，將對我們的收入產生不利影響。
與財務狀況相關的風險
我們的業務依賴於我們所服務產業的國內資本支出，資本支出減少可能對我們的流動性、營業成果及財務狀況造成重大不利影響。
我們可能因全球金融市場的不確定性或客戶財務狀況惡化及由此產生的信用風險而受到不利影響。
我們使用淨營業虧損（"NOL"）結轉的能力可能受到限制。
與監管事項相關的風險
我們受環境及職業健康與安全法規的約束，這可能使我們面臨重大成本與責任。
對永續性議題的關注度增加可能影響我們的業務。
許多州所頒布的反賠償條款可能限制或禁止一方對我們進行賠償。
適用稅法及規範之變更或面臨額外所得稅負擔，可能影響本公司之營運成果與現金流。
與本公司A類普通股相關之風險
本公司A類普通股之股價可能波動，您可能無法以原購入價格或更高價格將所持有之A類普通股重新出售。
paragraphs: 以下為影響本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流之特定風險因素。許多此等風險為本公司所無法控制。在評估本年度報告所包含之預測性陳述時，應考慮此等風險因素。上述所描述之風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨之唯一風險。若任何上述所描述之事件實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果及現金流造成不利影響，且本公司之結果可能與預期及歷史結果有重大差異，任何此等情況亦可能對本公司股票持有人造成不利影響。
本公司可能無法適應分散式電力技術以符合日益增加之客戶需求與電力負載，這可能會導致本公司電力發電服務之停機時間增加，並對客戶之電力供應造成中斷。
電力需求持續大幅超過來自電網之可用電力發電供應，例如油氣產業之電氣化，已對老化且不可靠之電力網造成壓力。此外，人工智慧之應用擴張，已導致現有資料中心之擴張及新資料中心之建設計畫。
隨著本公司擴展分散式電力服務，存在本公司現有服務可能無法有效管理相關電力負載之可能性，導致對客戶之停機時間與中斷。此等經驗可能因對本公司聲譽之損害及客戶之不滿意，對本公司業務與營運成果造成重大不利影響。若本公司無法適應電力發電技術以符合未來需求與客戶需求之演進，或無法達成其可靠性要求，本公司業務與營運成果可能受到不利影響。
分散式電力發電服務為客戶在電網接入不可用、成本高昂或延遲時之替代方案。若大型電力公用事業專案完成，並建立相關輸電與配電網路，本公司之分散式電力服務可能受到影響。在此情況下，客戶可能僅將本公司服務作為備用電力或過渡電力，直至電網電力恢復。
分散式電力產業之環境正快速演進，因多個終端市場之需求增加，包括資料中心與能源產業。因此，分散式電力產業內之競爭可能增加。若此情況實現，本公司 Power Solutions 分部所能佔據之總可達市場份額可能低於預期，這可能導致收入低於預期。
